title: Normalized localization descent of an inverse
statement: Let L:A→B localize W and let P be an iso-closed object property of B. Suppose F,G:B→C, H,I:A→C, b:L⋙F≅H, c:L⋙G≅I and a:H→I. For every representative X with P(LX), prescribe n_X:G(LX)≅F(LX) such that (b_X a_X c_X⁻¹)n_X=id. Then there is a unique natural isomorphism P.ι⋙G≅P.ι⋙F whose component on every such representative is n_X.

source.place: Expanded DAG clause 4, existing generic augmentation/localization proof; Mathlib mappingCocone.id_X and Localization.fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft.

proof.text: Descend b.hom≫a≫c.inv using full faithfulness of whiskering along L. The normalization identifies its inverse on representatives. Essential surjectivity and iso-closedness give invertibility on P; invert the restricted transformation. Naturality and essential surjectivity also give uniqueness.

mathlib_searches.query: A morphism into a mapping cocone is determined by its two component maps, and an isomorphism descends uniquely from a localization

The exact identity decomposition is in Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.MappingCocone.
Localization.Predicate defines the fully faithful whiskering functor. Local library search finds the complete generic proof already in the assigned module.

lean.statement:
theorem normalized_descent
    {A B C : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Category C]
    (L : A ⥤ B) (W : MorphismProperty A) [L.IsLocalization W]
    (P : ObjectProperty B) [P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
    (F G : B ⥤ C) (H I : A ⥤ C) (b : L ⋙ F ≅ H) (c : L ⋙ G ≅ I)
    (a : H ⟶ I) (n : ∀ X, P (L.obj X) → (G.obj (L.obj X) ≅ F.obj (L.obj X)))
    (hn : ∀ X (hX : P (L.obj X)),
      (b.hom.app X ≫ a.app X ≫ c.inv.app X) ≫ (n X hX).hom = 𝟙 _) :
    ∃! e : P.ι ⋙ G ≅ P.ι ⋙ F, ∀ X (hX : P (L.obj X)),
      e.hom.app ⟨L.obj X, hX⟩ = (n X hX).hom
